fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. God says, “…I will bring foreigners against you, the most ruthless of nations.” That's not a gentle description. When God names who is coming, He picks a hard word.
God doesn't point to a vote. He ends with, “For I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.” His own word is the reason He gives. The nations aren't named as the reason.

It's true, friend. The lament really does start with, “You were the seal of perfection, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.” Those are big words. Notice the "were," which looks back at what he used to be.

High priest sounds like a fine guess, friend, but it's not the title here. God says, “You were anointed as a guardian cherub, for I had ordained you.” That's the role the verse hands him. Picking a different job for him is like stamping the wrong shape into the dough.

The verse doesn't send him off to rule the seas, friend. God says, “So I drove you in disgrace from the mountain of God, and I banished you…” The words are driven and banished. That's a heavy part of the lament.

Yes, friend. God says, “so I cast you to the earth; I made you a spectacle before kings.” His heart grew proud of his beauty, and the verse follows that with the casting down. After that, he's made a spectacle before kings.
That's the reaction. God says, “All the nations who know you are appalled over you.” Appalled is a strong word. That's how the nations who know him respond to his end.
Rushing to take his place isn't in the verse, friend. God says, “All the nations who know you are appalled over you.” Appalled means shocked. That's the reaction the text gives.
Walls aren't mentioned here, friend. After “…I am against you, O Sidon…” God says, “…and I will be glorified within you.” That's the line to listen for. Rebuilding isn't part of it.
Lions and bears aren't in this verse, friend. Here God says, “…a pricking brier or a painful thorn…” Those are the plants He names for the trouble from the neighbors around Israel.
That's it. God says, “Then they will dwell in their own land, which I have given to My servant Jacob.” The land is described as already given. God says they will dwell there.
